sentences.text:
Nidhi Jindal vs Ankit Agarwal on 27 November, 2025
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. Of 2025
 (Arising Out Of Slp (Criminal) No. 5211 Of 2025)
 Nidhi Jindal 
 Versus
 Ankit Agarwal
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.

2. The High Court vide impugned order dated 19.02.2025 has set aside the order of the Family Court-cum-Trial Court dated 25.01.2023 whereby a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month was granted to the respondent-wife as interim maintenance.
It may be mentioned that the parties got married on 29.01.2020.

Unfortunately, the marital discord led to the initiation of cases, including registration of FIR No.75/2021 dated 12.04.2021 against the respondent-husband and his family members under Section 498A, 406, 323, 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, read with Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

3. Meanwhile, the appellant-wife filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. for maintenance before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Howrah, along with an affidavit giving details of her assets and liabilities.
She also filed a complaint under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is in these proceedings that the Trial Court granted interim maintenance of Rs.50,000/- per month in favour of the appellant- wife but the High Court has set aside the same on the ground that Reason:
the appellant has filed three different affidavits, thereby contradicting her own claim of monthly income and suppressing the material facts.
It was also noted that the appellant has sufficient financial income to maintain her expenses during the pendency of the matrimonial litigation.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it seems to us that both the reasons assigned by the High Court are contrary to law and record.

The High Court appears to have ignored the specific averments made by the appellant in her affidavit of assets and liabilities, where under the Head J, she has specifically disclosed the income/sources of income of the respondent-husband.

Keeping that income in view, the High Court was not expected to hold a roving enquiry on merits,
thereby assuming the role of the Trial Court while deciding the petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

1 5.
For the reasons aforestated, we allow this appeal.

The impugned judgment of the High Court dated 19.02.2025 is set aside, and the interim maintenance of Rs.50,000/- per month granted to the respondent-wife is restored in her favour from the date she filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C.

The respondent is directed to pay all the arrears along with interest @ 7 % per annum within a period of two months before the Trial Court, failing which the Trial Court shall take lawful coercive action to recover such arrears.
6. Similarly, the respondent shall be allowed to enter appearance and defend himself in the pending cases, only if he pays the monthly maintenance on or before the 10th day of each calendar month.
7. It is clarified that we have not expressed any opinion on the merits of the claim or counter-claim.
The Trial Court will decide the application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. as per its own merits and without being influenced by the observations made by this Court.
The appellant-wife is also awarded cost of Rs.25,000/- towards litigation expenses in this appeal.
That amount shall also be paid by the respondent-husband on the first date of appearance before the Family Court-cum-Trial Court.
